title: What Happens If You Stop Sleeping? Day 3 You Hallucinate (Sleep Deprivation)
description:
What happens if you stop sleeping? Sleep deprivation hits fast: by the third day without sleep, healthy people start to hallucinate.

Day by day:
- 24 hours awake: your performance is impaired about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10%, above the U.S. legal limit of 0.08% (CDC/NIOSH).
- 24-48 hours: perceptual distortions start: things look warped, colors and shapes seem off, time feels strange.
- 48-72 hours and beyond: complex hallucinations and disordered thinking; by the third day people report seeing, hearing and feeling things that aren't there (Waters et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2018).
- In 1963-64, 17-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for about 11 days (264 hours) for a science fair. Near the end he had serious memory problems. Afterward he slept 14 hours and 46 minutes and recovered fully.

Please don't try this: going without sleep for more than 48 hours is now considered unethical even in research. How long is the longest you've been awake?

Sources:
- Waters et al. (2018), Severe sleep deprivation causes hallucinations, Frontiers in Psychiatry: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6048360
- CDC/NIOSH, Driver fatigue on the job (24 hours awake = BAC 0.10): https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/motor-vehicle/driver-fatigue/index.html
- NPR (2024), Lessons from sleeplessness: Randy Gardner's record: https://www.npr.org/2024/01/28/1227217274/sleep-deprivation-record
- Scientific American, How long can humans stay awake?: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/how-long-can-humans-stay/

questions.q: What happens after 3 days without sleep?
questions.a: Studies of healthy volunteers show that by the third day without sleep most people experience hallucinations, often visual, auditory and tactile, plus confused thinking.

questions.q: Is 24 hours without sleep like being drunk?
questions.a: According to CDC/NIOSH, being awake for 24 hours impairs performance about as much as a blood alcohol concentration of 0.10%, above the U.S. legal limit of 0.08%.

questions.q: What is the longest anyone has stayed awake?
questions.a: Randy Gardner stayed awake about 11 days (264 hours) in 1963-64; longer claims exist, but Guinness stopped accepting attempts because they are dangerous.
